chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one in Ihram who listened to a man copulating with his wife, so he discharged (semen), he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him'.

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing upon him (no penalty/expitation due)
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram, a ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person in Ihram who listens to their spouse having intercourse and ejaculates?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that merely listening to one's wife during intercourse, even if it leads to ejaculation, does not incur the penalty of *dam* (sacrifice) typically associated with sexual acts in Ihram. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between active sexual engagement and passive auditory stimulation, emphasizing that the severity of the breach depends on the degree of physical or deliberate sexual act rather than mere sensory pleasure.
